corpus: IBM AMLworld HI-Small (synthetic, by IBM's own statement)
provenance: The 8,192 rows finance/real_2d.json draws, in the same order: a draw from the AMLworld temporal test window (the last 30 percent of transactions), enriched to 2 percent laundering, as the 114 inputs the published student takes before its own z-scoring: 32 per-account aggregates, 79 per-transaction window features and 3 pair features.
split: the rows of finance_aml.gbm's sample, a draw from the held-out temporal test window, the last 30 percent of the transactions in time order, enriched to 2 percent laundering
fit_note: finance_aml.student and its teacher finance_aml.gbm were fitted on the earlier training window (fit 56 percent, validation 14); neither was fitted, tuned or calibrated on these test-window rows.
attribution: Altman et al., 'Realistic Synthetic Financial Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering Models', NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. Data: IBM Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering (AML), CDLA-Sharing-1.0.
modifications: The 114 computed inputs per transaction of 8,192 test-window rows drawn with laundering enriched to 2 percent, rounded to 7 significant figures. Enhanced Data shared under the same CDLA-Sharing-1.0.

expected.note: The published student in plaintext on these rows, computed by this script with the shipped weights; the browser's plaintext reference must reproduce it. Rounding to 7 significant figures moves no decision: the largest logit shift against the student's published z-scored sample is 1.95e-05, below the smallest |logit| of 2.37e-03.
